requirement:
Habeas MUST provide built-in definitions named `habeas:<name>`, available in
every project without a declaration. Each built-in MUST have fixed text, which
states its obligations and is documented in Habeas's reference documentation, and
MUST state which reference roles may use it. References MUST resolve built-in
names alongside project definitions. So that every book stands alone, the book
MUST render a reference to a built-in as a badge without a link whose hover text
gives the built-in's full text. Built-ins MUST NOT require or permit evidence
files and MUST NOT appear in the requirements index, `habeas status`, or the
missing-evidence check of {cite}`requirements.ci.coverage`. A project definition
MUST NOT use a full name beginning with `habeas:`; validation MUST report one,
and the `:` character already makes such names invalid under
{cite}`requirements.ci.identifiers`. Validation MUST report a reference to a
built-in in a role the built-in does not permit, or that breaks the built-in's
stated form.
rationale:
## Judgment

The source and referenced tests satisfy `requirements.references.builtin_definitions`.

## Obligations and evidence

1. **Provide definitions named `habeas:<name>`; make them available in every project; require no declaration.** `src/builtins.rs#const[BUILTINS]` supplies `habeas:util`, and `src/builtins.rs#fn[builtin]` resolves it independently of project declarations. These are reachable from the marked rendering, validation, citation, and authoring roots. `src/builtins.rs#mod[tests]/fn[habeas_util_has_its_approved_text_and_permits_inline_or_fenced_citations]` checks lookup; the rendering and repository tests below exercise it in projects without a built-in declaration.

2. **Give each built-in fixed text; have that text state its obligations; document it in the reference documentation; state its permitted roles.** `src/builtins.rs#impl[Builtin]/fn[text]` embeds the approved text at compile time, while `src/builtins.rs#const[BUILTINS]` records the permitted role and `src/builtins.rs#impl[Builtin]/fn[check]` enforces it. The text describes the built-in's purpose and absence of obligations. `md/reference.md#section[How%20it%20works]/section[References]/section[Built-in%20definitions]` quotes the complete text and expressly permits only `{cite}`. `src/builtins.rs#mod[tests]/fn[habeas_util_has_its_approved_text_and_permits_inline_or_fenced_citations]` checks the text's identifying boundaries, equality with the documentation, permitted citation, and rejected implementation/test roles.

3. **Resolve built-in names alongside project definitions.** `src/evidence.rs#fn[validate_references]`, reached from the marked `inspect_repository_with_progress`, handles built-ins before project lookup. `src/lib.rs#fn[reference_badge]`, reached from the marked `replace_references`, likewise supports both kinds. `src/lib.rs#fn[reference_roles]` recognizes inline built-in names. Tests `tests/references.rs#fn[fenced_references_in_comments_and_built_in_rules_are_validated]` and `tests/references.rs#fn[built_ins_have_no_evidence_index_entry_or_status_and_are_validated_in_the_book]` exercise source and book resolution. `src/fenced.rs#mod[tests]/fn[opening_fences_take_a_role_and_one_valid_or_built_in_name]` additionally checks fenced-name recognition.

4. **Render book references as badges; omit links; give their full text on hover.** `src/lib.rs#fn[reference_badge]` produces a badge inside a `span` with the escaped full text in `title`, rather than an anchor. Both inline and fenced rendering reach this helper. `src/lib.rs#mod[tests]/fn[fenced_references_render_their_badge_and_body_and_built_ins_are_unlinked]` checks both paths, including full hover text and the absence of a link.

5. **Do not require evidence files; do not permit evidence files; exclude built-ins from the requirements index; exclude them from status; exclude them from the missing-evidence check.** Built-ins are separate from project declarations. `src/evidence.rs#fn[collect_definitions]` returns only project declarations, and `src/evidence.rs#fn[inspect_repository_with_progress]` uses those declarations for evidence matching and missing-evidence validation. A built-in evidence file consequently has no matching declaration and is reported as an orphan. `src/lib.rs#fn[preprocess_book]` similarly constructs index inputs from project declarations only; the reachable `src/index.rs#impl[DetailPlan]/fn[find]` and `src/index.rs#impl[DetailPlan]/fn[populate]` generate entries only for those inputs. The status caller, `src/commands.rs#fn[status_markdown_with_github]`, iterates the inspection's project definitions. The exclusion decision is therefore already made by the marked discovery root, not by an unreferenced status-specific built-in filter. `tests/references.rs#fn[built_ins_have_no_evidence_index_entry_or_status_and_are_validated_in_the_book]` asserts orphan rejection, no built-in definition/status/detail-page/index entry, and no missing-evidence finding. `tests/references.rs#fn[fenced_references_in_comments_and_built_in_rules_are_validated]` also asserts that valid built-in references require no evidence.

6. **Prohibit project full names beginning with `habeas:`; report them in validation; treat the colon as invalid under the cited identifier rule.** The reachable `src/evidence.rs#fn[collect_definitions]` reports reserved names and excludes them, with the general identifier check covering invalid names as well. `src/lib.rs#fn[preprocess_book]` excludes invalid full names from rendered definitions. `tests/references.rs#fn[project_definitions_cannot_use_reserved_built_in_names]` asserts the reserved-name diagnostic and exclusion from status.

7. **Report references using a forbidden role; report references breaking a built-in's stated form.** `src/evidence.rs#fn[validate_references]` calls `Builtin::check` and reports its error. The current built-in permits inline or fenced citations, with or without commentary, so it imposes no additional commentary/form constraint. The built-in unit test checks permitted and forbidden roles; the two repository tests above assert wrong-role diagnostics in source and book inputs. The fenced rendering test also verifies successful inline and fenced citations.

## Additional marked behavior

The built-in-specific citation-review exemption and Rust-item coverage behavior in `src/citations.rs#fn[citation_items]` and `src/rust_coverage.rs#fn[unreferenced_items]` are specified by the same items' `requirements.references.util` implementation references, rather than unspecified additions. The marked authoring preparation functions resolve cited built-ins to their fixed text; their referenced tests exercise declaration and site preparation. No unacknowledged gap was found.

text: :::{req} builtin_definitions
Habeas MUST provide built-in definitions named `habeas:<name>`, available in
every project without a declaration. Each built-in MUST have fixed text, which
states its obligations and is documented in Habeas's reference documentation, and
MUST state which reference roles may use it. References MUST resolve built-in
names alongside project definitions. So that every book stands alone, the book
MUST render a reference to a built-in as a badge without a link whose hover text
gives the built-in's full text. Built-ins MUST NOT require or permit evidence
files and MUST NOT appear in the requirements index, `habeas status`, or the
missing-evidence check of {cite}`requirements.ci.coverage`. A project definition
MUST NOT use a full name beginning with `habeas:`; validation MUST report one,
and the `:` character already makes such names invalid under
{cite}`requirements.ci.identifiers`. Validation MUST report a reference to a
built-in in a role the built-in does not permit, or that breaks the built-in's
stated form.
:::{req} coverage

Repository validation MUST check that every requirement defined by a fenced `{req}` directive in a chapter under the configured mdBook source directory has an evidence file named `evidence/<full-requirement-name>.json`, and MUST report each requirement whose evidence file is missing. The full name MUST use the chapter's path-derived namespace followed by the directive name; for example, a directive named `check` in `md/requirements.md` has the full name `requirements.check`.
:::{req} identifiers

Requirement and reference names MUST have nonempty dot-separated segments containing only ASCII letters, digits, underscores, or hyphens. A `{req}` directive whose full name is invalid, including one whose chapter path gives an invalid namespace, and a role with an invalid name MUST remain literal and MUST NOT define or reference a requirement. For nested chapter paths, a leading `reqs/` and a final `index` or `README` segment MUST be omitted from the requirement namespace.
:::{req} util
Habeas MUST provide the built-in `habeas:util` under
{cite}`requirements.references.builtin_definitions`, with this text:
> Cite this on an item that serves other code, including code outside the
> project such as a library calling a trait implementation it requires, and
> carries out no requirement or example itself: it has no obligations and no
> end-user-observable behavior of its own. A review that reaches it from a root judges what it does
> as part of that root.
Only `{cite}` MAY reference it, inline or fenced, with or without commentary. An
item whose only citations are of `habeas:util` MUST NOT need a citation review
under {cite}`requirements.references.citation_review`. A citation of
`habeas:util` MUST cover its item under
{cite}`requirements.references.rust_item_coverage`.
